candidates.name: Donavan McKinney
candidates.basis: Platform: tax billionaires, universal basic income, Medicare for All, codify abortion, end cash bail and qualified immunity, citizenship pathways, Green New Deal, tuition-free college.

candidates.name: T.P. Nykoriak
candidates.basis: No published policy positions found for this perennial candidate.

candidates.name: Brad Finstad
candidates.basis: Voted for One Big Beautiful Bill Act, backed Israel aid and 2026 Iran strikes, opposed war powers limits, all-of-the-above energy including oil and gas.

candidates.name: Jake Johnson
candidates.basis: Raise corporate taxes, fight monopolies, oppose tariffs, balanced budget amendment, oppose Medicaid and SNAP cuts, data center moratorium, right to repair.

candidates.name: Matt Little
candidates.basis: Wealth tax, Medicare for All, replace ICE, end military aid to Israel, Equality Act and abortion rights drove liberty, opposes data center expansion, backs police with accountability.

candidates.name: Eric Pratt
candidates.basis: Campaign stresses backing law enforcement, consistent law enforcement up to the border, and fighting fraud; few other stated positions.

candidates.name: Kelly Morrison
candidates.basis: Former OB-GYN who passed pro-choice legislation in Minnesota; abortion rights drove liberty score.

candidates.name: Tyler Bass
candidates.basis: Deport every illegal immigrant, oppose sanctuary policies and H-1B abuse, oppose gun restrictions (drove liberty), lower property taxes, risk-based private health coverage.

candidates.name: Betty McCollum
candidates.basis: Health care as a right, pro-union, pro-choice and LGBTQ rights and opposes concealed carry (liberty), renewable energy bills, public education, conditions on Israel aid.

photo.author: U.S. House Office of Photography (Franmarie Metzler)

candidates.name: Paul Wikstrom
candidates.basis: Eliminate estate tax and taxes on tips and overtime, cut regulations, expand child tax credit, cross-state insurance sales and price transparency.

candidates.name: Ilhan Omar
candidates.basis: $17 minimum wage, Medicare for All, free public college, LGBTQ and abortion rights (liberty), backed police abolition, opposed border funding, cutting military spending, opposed TikTok ban.

photo.file: File:Ilhan Omar, official portrait, 116th Congress (cropped) A.jpg
photo.author: U.S. House Office of Photography (Kristie Boyd)

candidates.name: John Nagel
candidates.basis: Cut taxes and spending, fund police, secure border with faster legal immigration, defend gun and speech rights (liberty), energy dominance, strong US leadership with allies.

candidates.name: Tom Emmer
candidates.basis: Sought to end state minimum wage, defund CFPB, repeal ACA, anti-abortion and opposed LGBTQ anti-bullying law (liberty), travel ban, pro-drilling, fights crypto regulation.

candidates.name: Doug Chapin
candidates.basis: Repeal tax cuts for the wealthy, Medicare for All or public option, abortion and LGBTQ rights and assault-weapon limits (liberty), citizenship pathways, restrict Israel aid, Paris Accords.

candidates.name: Michelle Fischbach
candidates.basis: Liberty averages repeated anti-abortion legislation with strong gun-rights support; voted for Israel support after October 7.

candidates.name: Erik Osberg
candidates.basis: Universal care goal and Medicare at 55, abortion rights plus background checks and red-flag laws (liberty), wind and solar investment, EPA enforcement, more public school funding.

candidates.name: Pete Stauber
candidates.basis: Authored bill ending Boundary Waters mineral withdrawal to allow copper-nickel mining and opposed Haaland over opposition to oil drilling.

candidates.name: Trina Swanson
candidates.basis: Antitrust enforcement and fair corporate taxes, universal healthcare, secure but humane border with earned citizenship, clean energy investment, protect Boundary Waters from mining.
